comparison: Perfect agreement on core analytical results (C2, C12-C14, C30-C31, C72). Both evaluations rate these mathematical proofs as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the rigorous proof structure, while peer reviewers explicitly praise the mathematical rigor and solid theoretical foundation.

Complete agreement on analytical result about external input eliminating oscillations (C15, C73). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the analytical proof, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the praised mathematical framework without specific concerns.

Full agreement on intuitive explanations (C20-C27). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes citation support and logical consistency, while peer reviewers specifically praise the intuition behind proofs as 'well explained' and 'helpful for readers.'

Significant disagreement on numerical simulations (C40-C47). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with clear documentation, but peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to concerns about delay effects being ignored and questions about biological relevance of the parameter choices.

Major disagreement on motif enumeration (C18-C19, C53-C55, C84-C85). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED as straightforward graph theory application, but peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether motif decomposition is 'too simplistic' for brain networks and noting the odd/even rule is 'far from reality.'

Partial disagreement on lesion simulations (C56-C63, C69). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with clear results, but peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the simulations while questioning biological applicability and noting the approach is 'too theoretical without real application for brain dynamics.' However, one reviewer notes it provides testable predictions.

Agreement on spiking neuron validation (C66-C68). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED (noting C70 is speculative), while peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED with qualification that 'results are less clear' but provide 'additional layers of confidence.' Both acknowledge these as more biologically realistic.

Disagreement on limitations acknowledgment (C74-C77). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for appropriate scientific caution, but peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting that while authors addressed delay concerns in revisions, the treatment remains incomplete and delays are still largely ignored.

Agreement on broader applicability claims (C94-C96). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations and qualified speculation, while peer reviewers accept broad applicability as a strength without challenge.

Partial overlap on conclusions about STN necessity (C86-C89 in OpenEval R9, C56-C63, C69, C86-C89 in Peer R6). OpenEval rates conclusions as SUPPORTED by simulations, while peer reviewers rate the underlying simulations as UNCERTAIN due to biological relevance concerns, though they acknowledge testable predictions.

Partial overlap on rodent-specific speculation (C70). OpenEval notes this is appropriately acknowledged as hypothesis in R7 (SUPPORTED overall), while peer reviewers in R9 treat speculative claims (C70, C90) as reasonable interpretations (SUPPORTED), noting they provide testable predictions.

Agreement on recommendations (C90). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED noting it represents future work, while peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, treating it as reasonable interpretation that provides testable predictions.

Disagreement on conceptual framework (C78-C82 in OpenEval, C71, C80-C82 in Peer). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of rigorous demonstration of scalability claims, while peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN but focus on practical applicability concerns, noting the odd/even rule is 'too strict' and weight distributions matter.

Partial overlap on contextualization (C71, C91-C93 in OpenEval vs C71, C80-C82 in Peer). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED for appropriate contextualization, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN focusing on the practical applicability of the topology-focused framework.
